examples.description: The most common cystic fibrosis-causing variant worldwide: an in-frame deletion of three bases (CTT) removing a single phenylalanine at position 508 of the CFTR protein. The protein is made but misfolds and is largely degraded before reaching the cell surface.

A two-base deletion early in BRCA1, historically written 185delAG, one of the founder variants described in Ashkenazi Jewish populations. The deletion shifts the reading frame near the start of the protein.
examples.disease: Hereditary breast and ovarian cancer syndrome

examples.description: The sickle cell variant: a single A to T substitution (c.20A>T) in the GAG codon of beta globin changes a glutamic acid to a valine, producing haemoglobin S which polymerises when deoxygenated. It is historically called Glu6Val after the mature beta chain, in which the initiator methionine is cleaved; counted from the initiator methionine as HGVS requires, the residue is position 7.

The classic achondroplasia variant: a glycine to arginine substitution at position 380 in the transmembrane domain of FGFR3, causing constitutive receptor activation. Nearly all cases of achondroplasia carry this or the adjacent c.1138G>C change at the same codon.
An X-linked red cell enzyme deficiency included here as a disease-area example only; no single variant is asserted in this entry.

label: Illustrative worked examples bundled with Omevra. Well-known textbook variants, included to demonstrate the software. Not a clinical database and not a source of classifications for real patients.
